SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: We will practise the speech sounds 'k' and 'g' through games each week.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: the sounds that make up words

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Exercises to strengthen or coordinate the lips, tongue and jaw.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Please do the oral motor exercises we practised, ten times each, twice a day.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: exercises for the lips, tongue and jaw

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Keeping the mouth, teeth and gums clean.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Good oral hygiene lowers the risk of infection, so please brush his teeth after every meal.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: keeping the mouth and teeth clean

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Advice to wait patiently while a person forms a reply.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: When you ask a question, give him extra time to answer before repeating it.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: wait a little longer for him to reply

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Advice to lower distracting sounds so speech is easier to follow.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: It helps to reduce background noise, such as turning off the television, before you talk.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: make the room quieter before talking

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A request for someone to explain something without repeating the clinician's wording.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Could you tell me in your own words how you will thicken his drinks at home?
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: explain it back to me your way

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A standard opening line for a referral letter.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: I am writing to refer Mrs Lee, aged 72, for an instrumental swallowing assessment.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: I am asking you to see this patient

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.term: I would be grateful if you could
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A polite formal way to make a request in a letter.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: I would be grateful if you could review his hearing before our next appointment.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: please could you

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A phrase introducing findings from the most recent appointment.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: On review today, Jack's speech was understood by unfamiliar listeners most of the time.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: when I saw them today

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A phrase reporting gradual, consistent improvement.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Since starting therapy, Ella has made steady progress with her sentence length.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: has been slowly getting better

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A formal phrase stating that support is still needed.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: He continues to require supervision at all meals because of his impulsive eating.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: still needs

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A formal phrase linking a letter to an earlier communication.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Further to my letter of 3 March, I enclose the results of Sam's language assessment.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: following on from

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.term: please do not hesitate to contact me
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A polite closing line offering further help.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: If you have any questions about her plan, please do not hesitate to contact me.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: please get in touch if you need to

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: To communicate and coordinate with another person or service.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: I will liaise with the school's special educational needs coordinator about classroom support.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: talk to and work with

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Because of, or taking into account, particular information.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: In light of his recent chest infection, I have advised a further swallow review.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: because of

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A phrase directing the reader to details later in a document.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: The recommendations outlined below should be followed at all meals.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: listed further down

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A later visit to check progress after earlier care.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: A follow-up appointment has been arranged for six weeks to review her voice.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: another visit to see how things are going

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: To formally end a patient's episode of care with a service.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: As her goals have now been met, discharge from the service is planned for the end of this month.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: finish therapy with us

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Advice to put only a little food in the mouth at a time.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Please offer small mouthfuls and check his mouth is empty before giving more.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: small bites, one at a time

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A phrase that recognises a person's concern before giving information.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: I understand this is worrying, but many children with similar difficulties make good progress.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: I know this is hard to hear

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: A person's informed agreement to an assessment or treatment.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Before the camera test, I will explain it fully and ask for your consent.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: your agreement to go ahead

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: Therapy appointments happening at set, repeated intervals.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Attending regular sessions and practising at home will give him the best chance of improving.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: appointments at the same time each week or fortnight

SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.definition: To act or speak one after another in an activity or conversation.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.example: Games where you take turns help Leo learn to wait and listen in conversation.
SPEECH_PATHOLOGY.plain: each person has a go, one after another

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Describing a disease that can pass between animals and people.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Because ringworm is zoonotic, the owner was advised to wear gloves when handling the kitten.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A pus-filled infection of the womb, mainly in unspayed females.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The unspayed bitch was diagnosed with pyometra and taken to surgery the same evening.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A life-threatening condition where the stomach fills with gas and twists, mainly in large deep-chested dogs.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The Great Dane presented with a swollen abdomen and retching, consistent with gastric dilatation-volvulus.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Breathing problems in short-nosed breeds caused by narrowed nostrils and excess soft tissue.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome increases anaesthetic risk, so recovery was closely supervised.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A tear of a key stabilising ligament inside the dog's knee joint.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Cranial cruciate ligament rupture was suspected because the tibia moved forward abnormally on examination.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Abnormal development of the hip joint leading to looseness and later arthritis.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Radiographs confirmed hip dysplasia in the young retriever, explaining his reluctance to climb stairs.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Long-term, gradual loss of kidney function, common in older cats.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Chronic kidney disease was staged using blood and urine results, and a renal diet was started.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Overactivity of the thyroid gland, causing weight loss despite a good appetite.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Hyperthyroidism was confirmed in the twelve-year-old cat, which had lost weight while eating ravenously.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A disorder where the body cannot control blood sugar because of insulin problems.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Diabetes mellitus was diagnosed after glucose was found in the dog's urine and blood.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal glands, which may cause collapse.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Hypoadrenocorticism should be considered in young dogs with vague, recurring gastrointestinal signs.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal glands, often causing thirst, hunger and a pot belly.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The terrier's pot-bellied appearance and hair loss raised suspicion of hyperadrenocorticism.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A highly contagious virus causing severe vomiting and bloody diarrhoea, especially in puppies.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The unvaccinated puppy tested positive for parvovirus and was admitted to the isolation ward.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Blockage of the tube that carries urine out of the bladder.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The male cat straining in the litter tray had a urethral obstruction and needed urgent catheterisation.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A group of conditions affecting a cat's bladder and urethra.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Stress and low water intake are linked to feline lower urinary tract disease in indoor cats.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Inflammation of the outer ear canal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Recurrent otitis externa in the spaniel was thought to be linked to an underlying skin allergy.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An inherited tendency to itchy skin inflammation triggered by environmental allergens.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Atopic dermatitis was diagnosed once parasites and food reactions had been ruled out.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Itching that makes an animal scratch, lick or chew its skin.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Severe pruritus had caused self-inflicted wounds on the dog's flanks.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A parasite that lives on the skin or coat, such as a flea, tick or mite.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: An ectoparasite burden was found on coat brushings, so the household's other pets were also treated.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A parasite that lives inside the body, such as a worm.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Faecal testing helps target endoparasite treatment rather than worming every animal routinely.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A medicine that kills or removes parasitic worms.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Overuse of a single anthelmintic class has contributed to resistance in sheep flocks.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: The ability of microbes to survive medicines that would normally kill them.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Antimicrobial resistance threatens both animal and human health, so culture is advised before treatment.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Careful, responsible use of antimicrobial drugs to keep them effective.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The practice's antimicrobial stewardship policy restricts certain drugs to cases with culture results.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Surgical removal of the ovaries and uterus.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Ovariohysterectomy eliminates the risk of pyometra and was booked for after her season.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Surgical removal of the testicles in a male animal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Castration was recommended to reduce roaming and prostate problems in the young dog.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Drugs given before anaesthesia to calm the animal and reduce pain.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Premedication was given thirty minutes before induction, and the dog settled quietly in his kennel.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Use of drugs to make an animal calm or drowsy without full anaesthesia.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Light sedation allowed the radiographs to be taken without stressing the anxious cat.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Relief of pain, or the medicines used to provide it.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Multimodal analgesia was planned to keep the patient comfortable after the fracture repair.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A scale for judging an animal's fat cover by looking and feeling.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Her body condition score was high, so a weight management plan was discussed with the owner.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: How quickly colour returns to the gums after pressing them, reflecting circulation.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A prolonged capillary refill time and pale gums suggested the dog was in shock.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A test of hydration where lifted skin is watched as it falls back.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A slow skin tent indicated moderate dehydration, so intravenous fluids were started.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Listening to the heart, lungs or gut with a stethoscope.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Auscultation revealed a heart murmur that had not been noted at the previous vaccination.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Examining the body by feeling with the hands.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Abdominal palpation detected a firm mass in the cranial abdomen.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Laboratory analysis of blood cells, such as red and white cell counts.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Haematology showed anaemia, so the vet looked for a source of blood loss.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Blood tests measuring chemicals that reflect organ function.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Serum biochemistry revealed raised liver enzymes in the older Labrador.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Laboratory examination of a urine sample.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Urinalysis showed dilute urine, supporting the owner's report that the cat was drinking more.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An X-ray image of part of the body.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A thoracic radiograph was taken to check for spread of the tumour to the lungs.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Imaging using high-frequency sound waves to view internal organs.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Abdominal ultrasonography identified fluid around the spleen.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A sample of cells drawn from a lump through a thin needle.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A fine-needle aspirate of the skin lump was sent for cytology.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Examination of individual cells under a microscope.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Cytology suggested a benign fatty lump, but monitoring for growth was advised.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Removal of a small piece of tissue to examine it in a laboratory.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A biopsy of the gut wall was taken to distinguish inflammation from lymphoma.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Abnormal, uncontrolled growth of tissue, which may be benign or malignant.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Neoplasia remained on the list of differentials until the biopsy result came back.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A cancer of the lymphocytes, often causing enlarged lymph nodes.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Several enlarged lymph nodes led to a suspicion of lymphoma in the middle-aged boxer.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An uncertain outlook in which recovery is possible but by no means assured.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Given the severity of the toxin exposure, a guarded prognosis was given to the owner.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Deliberately ending an animal's life painlessly to prevent further suffering.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: After discussing his declining quality of life, the family chose euthanasia at home.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An overall judgement of an animal's comfort, enjoyment and ability to function.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A quality of life checklist helped the owner track good and bad days.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: The everyday care, housing and management of animals.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Poor husbandry, including incorrect heating, explained the reptile's metabolic bone disease.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A disease that must, by law, be reported to the government authorities.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Suspected foot-and-mouth is a notifiable disease, so the vet reported it immediately.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Measures that prevent disease entering or spreading within animal populations.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Biosecurity on the farm included foot dips and quarantine for newly bought cattle.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Planned care focused on preventing disease across a whole group of farm animals.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The herd health plan scheduled vaccinations, mobility scoring and fertility checks across the year.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Inflammation of the udder or mammary gland, usually from infection.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Clinical mastitis was detected at milking when clots appeared in the milk from one quarter.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Difficult or obstructed birth.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The heifer had dystocia because the calf was too large, and a caesarean was performed.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Abdominal pain in horses, ranging from mild to life-threatening.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The horse showed colic signs, pawing and rolling, so a rectal examination was carried out.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Painful inflammation of tissue within the hoof, common in overweight horses and ponies.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Laminitis was diagnosed in the overweight pony after it was turned out on rich spring grass.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An abnormal gait caused by pain or dysfunction in a limb.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The degree of lameness was graded at walk and trot before nerve blocks were performed.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Not advisable because it could cause harm in a particular situation.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Anti-inflammatory drugs were contraindicated because of the cat's reduced kidney function.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: The rate at which new cases of a condition occur in a population.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The incidence of tick-borne disease in dogs has risen as pets travel abroad more often.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: The passing of an infection from one animal or person to another.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Transmission of the virus occurs through direct contact with infected faeces.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A fixed set of steps to follow in a particular clinical situation.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The isolation protocol requires staff to wear gowns and gloves for every patient contact.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A measurable value used to describe or monitor a condition.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Heart rate, temperature and blood pressure were the main parameters monitored under anaesthesia.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A list of possible conditions that could explain an animal's signs, narrowed down by testing.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The differential diagnosis for the vomiting cat included foreign body, pancreatitis and kidney disease.

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Everyday word for neutering a female animal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: We often suggest spaying about three months after her first season, but the best timing depends on her breed and size — we'll advise you.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: an operation so a female pet cannot have babies

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An operation that stops an animal from being able to breed.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Neutering can reduce roaming and some behaviour problems in male cats.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: an operation so your pet cannot have babies or father them

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Giving treatment to get rid of internal worms.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Regular worming is important for Bella, especially as she lives with young children.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: medicine to get rid of worms

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Products used to kill fleas on a pet and in the home.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please apply the flea treatment to all the pets in your house, not just Max.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: medicine to kill fleas

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A repeat vaccine given to keep immunity at a protective level.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Milo is due his booster vaccination next month, so we will send you a reminder.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a top-up vaccine

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Taking a small blood sample to check health and organ function.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: A blood test before the anaesthetic helps us check her kidneys and liver are working well.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a small sample of blood to check how the body is working

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Everyday word for a swelling or mass under or on the skin.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: I'd like to take a few cells from this lump so we know what it is.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a swelling you can see or feel

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Keeping an animal confined to a crate or small pen to let an injury heal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: After the spinal injury, he will need strict cage rest for four weeks.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: keeping him in a crate or small space so he does not move about

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An instruction to exercise a dog only on a lead, without running free.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: For the next six weeks, lead walks only, please, and no jumping on furniture.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: walks on the lead only, no running off the lead

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A cone-shaped collar that stops an animal reaching a wound.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please keep the Elizabethan collar on until the stitches are removed.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a cone around the neck to stop licking or biting the wound

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: To deliberately not give food for a set time, for example before anaesthesia.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please withhold food from 10 p.m. the night before, but leave water down.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: do not give any food

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Fully unconscious and pain-free because of anaesthetic drugs.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The dental work will be done under general anaesthetic, and she can go home the same day.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: fully asleep during the procedure

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An informal way to say an animal is not eating normally.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: You mentioned he's been off his food since Tuesday; has he been drinking normally?
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: not eating as much as usual

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for drinking excessive amounts of water.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Polydipsia was reported by the owner, who had to refill the water bowl several times daily.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: drinking much more than normal

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for producing abnormally large volumes of urine.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Polyuria and increased thirst in an older cat can point to kidney or thyroid disease.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: passing much more urine than usual

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for reduced or absent appetite.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Inappetence for more than a day in a rabbit needs urgent attention.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: not wanting to eat

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for vomiting.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Emesis was induced shortly after the dog swallowed the chocolate.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: being sick

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for a raised body temperature.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Pyrexia was recorded on admission, which suggests an infection.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a high temperature

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Unusually tired, slow and lacking energy.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: If she becomes lethargic or stops eating, please bring her straight back in.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: very tired and not her usual self

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Medical term for hair loss.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The alopecia on his tail is likely to be caused by a flea allergy.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: patches of hair loss

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Affecting both the left and right sides.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The bilateral ear infection means we need to treat both ears every day.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: on both sides

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Either of the back legs of a four-legged animal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: She is lame on the left hind limb, so we will start with an X-ray of the knee.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: back leg

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A structured plan of diet and exercise to help an animal reach a healthy weight.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Let's agree a weight management plan and weigh Charlie every month.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a plan of food and exercise to help your pet lose weight safely

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A special food recommended by the vet to manage a medical condition.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The prescribed diet is lower in phosphorus, which helps protect her kidneys.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: special food the vet recommends for this illness

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: To watch something carefully for any change.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please keep an eye on the wound and call us if it becomes red or swollen.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: watch carefully

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A phrase introducing warning signs that need urgent attention.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Contact us immediately if he tries to vomit without bringing anything up.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: ring us straight away if

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A follow-up visit to see how a problem is responding to treatment.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: I've booked a recheck appointment in ten days to look at the stitches.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a visit to check how things are healing

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: An approximate figure for the cost of planned treatment.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Before we go ahead, I'll give you a written estimate for the surgery and aftercare.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: how much it is likely to cost

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A document an owner signs to agree to a procedure.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please read the consent form carefully and ask if anything is unclear before signing.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a form you sign to say you agree to the treatment

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Care that focuses on comfort and quality of life rather than cure.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Palliative care can keep Rosie comfortable at home for as long as she is enjoying life.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: care to keep your pet comfortable, not to cure the illness

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A gentle everyday phrase for euthanasia of an animal.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: If you decide to have him put to sleep, you are welcome to stay with him.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: ending your pet's life peacefully and painlessly

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A compassionate phrase for introducing bad news.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: I'm sorry to tell you that the scan shows the tumour has spread.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: I have some sad news

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A phrase used in letters to report that choices were explained to the owner.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: We discussed the options of surgery or medical management, and Mrs Brown chose surgery.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: we talked about the choices

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A courteous opening for a referral letter to a colleague.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Thank you for seeing Bruno, a seven-year-old Labrador with a persistent cough.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: thank you for agreeing to examine

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A phrase stating the purpose of a referral is more tests.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: I am referring Daisy for further investigation of her recurrent seizures.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: for more tests

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A phrase introducing past or ongoing problems in a case summary.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Luna has a history of intermittent diarrhoea over the past four months.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: has had

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: A tiny implanted identification device that a scanner can read.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Please update the contact details linked to his microchip now that you have moved.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a tiny ID tag under the skin

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Written guidance on caring for an animal after it goes home.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: The discharge instructions explain when to give her medicine and when to come back.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: notes on how to look after your pet at home

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Everyday word for an ultrasound or other imaging test.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: We'll do a scan of his tummy to look at the organs in more detail.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: a painless test that shows pictures of the inside of the body

VETERINARY_SCIENCE.definition: Heavier than is healthy for the animal's size and breed.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.example: Being overweight puts extra strain on her joints, so losing a little will help.
VETERINARY_SCIENCE.plain: carrying too much weight
